On September 2, 2026, SoundHound AI, Inc. completed its acquisition of LivePerson, Inc. through two merger subsidiaries, Lightspeed Merger Sub Inc. and Lightspeed Merger Sub II Inc., under an Amended and Restated Merger Agreement dated July 2, 2026. At the same closing, SoundHound entered into a registration rights agreement with the holders of LivePerson's First Lien Convertible Senior Notes due 2029 and 10.0% Second Lien Senior Subordinated Secured Notes due 2029, and it consummated the notes restructuring transactions under the Notes Restructuring Agreement dated April 21, 2026. SoundHound also appointed John Collins as Chief Financial Officer effective upon the merger closing.

Under the merger, each share of LivePerson common stock, par value $0.001, converted into the right to receive 0.4673 shares of SoundHound Class A Common Stock, except shares held through the Tel-Aviv Stock Exchange Clearing House Ltd., which received $3.31 in cash per share. LivePerson stock options and warrants were cancelled for no consideration, and restricted stock units were either settled for the merger consideration or assumed and converted into SoundHound awards. In the notes restructuring, the holder of the First Lien Secured Notes accepted 25,142,335 shares of SoundHound common stock and $2,499,450 in cash in full satisfaction of LivePerson's obligations, and the holders of the Second Lien Secured Notes accepted 11,752,504 shares and $3,348,550 in cash. The Second Lien notes carry a 10.0% interest rate and both note series mature in 2029. The filing does not state what specific assets secure the notes, only that they are first lien and second lien secured notes, and it does not state any fees or guarantees. The shares issued to the note holders were issued in reliance on Section 4(a)(2) of the Securities Act as a transaction not involving a public offering. The registration rights agreement requires SoundHound to file a resale shelf registration statement for the shares issued to the note holders and to use reasonable best efforts to keep it effective.

The filing states that the merger and notes restructuring were completed and announced on September 4, 2026. The notes restructuring satisfied LivePerson's obligations under the secured notes by giving the note holders SoundHound common stock and cash instead of repayment, and the merger converted LivePerson stockholders into SoundHound stockholders. The filing does not state that any proceeds are being used for AI infrastructure spending or provide any capital expenditure figures, so a reader cannot determine the impact on AI infrastructure spending from this filing alone.

On June 16, 2026, Space Exploration Technologies Corp., X67 Inc., a wholly owned subsidiary of Space Exploration Technologies Corp., and Anysphere, Inc., which the filing calls Cursor, entered into an Agreement and Plan of Merger. The merger became effective on August 14, 2026. X67 Inc. merged with and into Cursor, and Cursor survived as a wholly owned subsidiary of Space Exploration Technologies Corp.

Under the merger agreement, the shares of Cursor common stock and preferred stock outstanding immediately before the effective time were converted into the right to receive an aggregate of 389,289,254 shares of Space Exploration Technologies Corp. Class A common stock. This was based on an implied equity value of Cursor of $60.0 billion and a price per share equal to the volume weighted average closing price over the seven consecutive trading days immediately before the closing. Vested Cursor restricted stock units, which are promises to deliver shares once vesting conditions are met, were converted into the right to receive an aggregate of 1,752,426 shares of Class A common stock before any tax withholding. Unvested Cursor restricted stock units and Cursor stock options were assumed and converted into approximately 29,128,326 restricted stock units and approximately 44,365,047 stock options to purchase Class A common stock. Cash received in lieu of fractional shares was also part of the merger consideration, but the filing does not state the amount. The filing does not state an interest rate, fees, a maturity date, security, or a guarantee. The shares were issued in reliance on the exemption from registration under Section 4(a)(2) of the Securities Act of 1933, as a transaction by an issuer not involving any public offering.

The filing does not state what the merger consideration will be used for or what the strategic purpose of the merger is. It also does not state how the merger relates to AI infrastructure spending. The only stated effect is that Cursor became a wholly owned subsidiary of Space Exploration Technologies Corp. Therefore the filing provides no information about AI infrastructure spending beyond the completion of this acquisition.

On June 8, 2026, Novanta Inc., Novanta Medical Technologies Corp. as Buyer, Novanta Corporation as Intermediate Parent, Runway Midco, LLC as Seller, and Runway Buyer, LLC entered into an Equity Purchase Agreement. Buyer agreed to acquire from Seller all of the issued and outstanding limited liability company interests of Runway Buyer. The closing occurred on July 23, 2026. At closing, the Buyer Parties paid Seller approximately $1.2 billion in cash, subject to customary adjustments for cash, working capital, debt and transaction expenses. A milestone payment of $250.0 million remains payable by the Buyer Parties to Seller on or before January 8, 2027.

To fund the acquisition, on July 22, 2026, Intermediate Parent borrowed $616.0 million in total under its revolving credit facility and delayed draw term loan facility under the Fourth Amended and Restated Credit Agreement. A revolving credit facility is a line of credit that can be borrowed, repaid and borrowed again. A delayed draw term loan is a committed loan that the borrower can draw in stages, and here it was drawn to help pay for the acquisition. The filing does not state the interest rate, fees, security or any guarantee for these borrowings. The borrowings are due when the Credit Agreement matures in June 2030 and may be repaid at any time before maturity without a prepayment penalty. The remaining consideration was funded with cash on hand. After these borrowings, Novanta's consolidated debt totals $854.7 million.

The filing states that the $616.0 million borrowing was made to fund the Transaction, and the rest of the purchase price was paid from cash on hand. The filing does not describe Runway Buyer's business or any connection to AI infrastructure, so it provides no information about AI infrastructure spending. It shows only that Novanta used a combination of new debt and existing cash to complete the acquisition and that its consolidated debt increased to $854.7 million.

On June 22, 2026, Quantum Computing Inc., a Delaware corporation, entered into a Stock Purchase Agreement with NHanced Semiconductors, Inc., a Delaware corporation, the Gretchen Louise Trinklein Patti Revocable Trust, the Robert Steve Patti Revocable Trust, the Robert Steve Patti Irrevocable Trust, Gretchen Trinklein Patti and Robert Patti as beneficial owners, and Robert Patti as seller representative. Under the agreement, Quantum Computing Inc. agreed to acquire all of the issued and outstanding shares of common stock of NHanced Semiconductors, Inc. The transaction closed on June 22, 2026, and NHanced became a wholly owned subsidiary of Quantum Computing Inc.

The aggregate purchase price consists of $68.1 million in cash, subject to adjustments for unpaid transaction expenses, closing indebtedness, closing cash and working capital surplus or deficit, plus a number of shares of Quantum Computing Inc. common stock equal to $5.0 million divided by the volume weighted average price of the common stock for the 30 trading days ending five trading days prior to closing. At closing, $20.0 million of the cash was deposited into an interest bearing escrow account as a holdback, payable to the sellers or returned to the company based on whether NHanced achieves specified total revenue thresholds for the years ending December 31, 2027 and December 31, 2028. The sellers may also receive earnout payments of up to $72.0 million in two tranches: up to $20.0 million, consisting of up to $10.0 million for each of the periods January 1, 2027 through December 31, 2027 and January 1, 2028 through December 31, 2028, based on specified total revenue thresholds and, for the 2028 period, alternatively specified total EBITDA thresholds, and up to $52.0 million based on further specified total revenue and EBITDA thresholds over the same periods. Earnout payments may be made in cash and/or company common stock at the sellers' election, but the stock component of any payment may not exceed 50% of that payment without the company's prior written consent. Any shares issued as earnout consideration are valued using the volume weighted average price for the 30 trading days ending five trading days prior to the applicable payment date. If the company has filed an automatic shelf registration statement on Form S-3ASR, any seller holding shares issued under the agreement may request a prospectus supplement covering resale, which the company will file within 15 days, but the company has no obligation to file or maintain such a registration statement.

The filing states that following the closing, NHanced is expected to continue supporting its existing customers and partners while contributing to the Company's manufacturing and commercialization initiatives. This indicates that the acquisition is intended to strengthen the Company's production and go-to-market capabilities, as described in the filing. The filing does not mention AI infrastructure spending specifically, but the stated purpose of the transaction is to expand manufacturing and commercialization, which suggests an investment in hardware related capabilities.

On May 29, 2026, Richtech Robotics Inc., a Nevada corporation, completed the purchase of an approximately 79,325 square foot building located at 9530 S. Rainbow Blvd., Las Vegas, Nevada 89139. The seller was PSIF EBS Rainbow LLC, a Delaware limited liability company. The purchase was made under a purchase and sale agreement dated April 1, 2026. On May 15, 2026, Richtech Robotics assigned its rights and obligations under that agreement to Richtech Rainbow Holdings LLC, a Nevada limited liability company and wholly owned subsidiary, and the purchase was completed through that subsidiary.

The purchase price was $21,180,000.00, paid with the Company's cash on hand. The filing does not state any interest rate, fees, maturity date, pledged security, or guarantee because this was a cash purchase, not a loan.

The Company intends to use the property as a strategic U.S. based facility for warehousing, assembly and light manufacturing, as well as research and development, testing, and robotics driven data collection and model training to support the continuous improvement of the Company's robotics and AI systems. This shows that Richtech Robotics is spending its own cash on physical space for AI related work, including collecting data and training models for its robots.

On May 11, 2026, Coursera, Inc., a Delaware public benefit corporation, completed its previously announced combination with Udemy, Inc., a Delaware corporation, under the Agreement and Plan of Merger dated December 17, 2025. The parties to that agreement were Udemy, Coursera, and Chess Merger Sub, Inc., a Delaware corporation and direct wholly owned subsidiary of Coursera. Chess Merger Sub merged with and into Udemy, and Udemy continued as the surviving corporation and as a wholly owned subsidiary of Coursera.

The merger was a stock for stock transaction, not a loan, so the filing reports no interest rate, fees, maturity date, pledged security, or guarantee. Each share of Udemy common stock, par value $0.00001 per share, outstanding immediately before the effective time, except certain shares owned by Coursera, Udemy, or Merger Sub, was converted into the right to receive 0.800 shares of Coursera common stock, par value $0.00001 per share, plus cash in lieu of fractional shares. For outstanding Udemy stock options and stock appreciation rights, the filing defines a Merger Consideration Value as the product of $4.78, the average closing price of Coursera common stock for the five full trading days before the closing date, multiplied by the 0.800 exchange ratio. Udemy restricted stock unit awards were assumed and converted into Coursera restricted stock unit awards using the same 0.800 exchange ratio, with director awards vesting fully at the effective time. Also on May 11, 2026, before the effective time, Coursera amended its certificate of incorporation to increase authorized shares of common stock from 300,000,000 to 600,000,000.

The filing does not state a purpose for the merger or any use of funds, and it contains no information about AI infrastructure spending. Because the consideration is Coursera common stock rather than cash, the transaction does not involve borrowing or new cash outlays described in the filing. The only stated corporate action tied to the merger is the increase in authorized shares from 300,000,000 to 600,000,000. A reader looking for AI infrastructure spending will find nothing in this filing about that topic.

On February 2, 2026, Quantum Computing Inc. completed its acquisition of all issued and outstanding shares of common stock of Luminar Semiconductor, Inc., a Delaware corporation, from Luminar Technologies, Inc., a Delaware corporation. The acquisition was made under a Stock Purchase Agreement dated December 15, 2025, which Quantum Computing Inc. had previously disclosed and filed with the SEC.

The consideration paid at closing consisted of approximately $97.5 million in cash plus $11.0 million that had been placed with an escrow agent when the Stock Purchase Agreement was signed. The $11.0 million escrowed amount will remain with the escrow agent until February 2, 2027 to cover certain limited indemnification obligations of the seller under the Stock Purchase Agreement. The filing does not state an interest rate, fees, a maturity date, any security or pledge of assets, or any guarantee in connection with the transaction.

The filing states that the agreement was for the acquisition of all shares of Luminar Semiconductor, Inc. and that Quantum Computing Inc. will file the target's financial statements and pro forma financial information as an amendment to the Form 8-K no later than 71 calendar days after the required filing date. The filing's forward looking statements refer to anticipated benefits including integration of the target's products and technologies and acceleration of the Company's development roadmap, but the filing does not state that the acquisition is for AI infrastructure spending or provide any figures on AI infrastructure.

Lumen Technologies, Inc. and the Sellers named therein agreed to sell the Mass Markets fiber-to-the-home business in 11 states to Forged Fiber 37, LLC. The purchase agreement is dated May 21, 2025, and AT&T DW Holdings, Inc. is a party solely for purposes of Section 11.16 of that agreement. The current report is dated February 2, 2026.

The filing does not state the purchase price, interest rate, fees, maturity, security, or guarantee for the sale itself. The only amount given is that on and after the closing date, the company plans to apply approximately $4.8 billion of the proceeds from the transaction and cash on hand to redeem all outstanding 10.000% secured notes due 2032, 4.125% super-priority senior secured notes due 2030, and 4.125% super-priority senior secured notes due 2029 at the applicable redemption price and pay accrued and unpaid interest, repay all outstanding term loans due under its Superpriority Revolving/Term Loan A Credit Agreement, and repay all outstanding amounts due under its Superpriority Term B Credit Agreement.

The filing states that the company plans to use approximately $4.8 billion of the proceeds from the transaction and cash on hand to redeem and repay debt. It does not state any use of the proceeds for AI infrastructure spending. The only stated purpose is to reduce outstanding secured notes and super-priority loans.

On January 27, 2026, Serve Robotics Inc. completed its acquisition of Diligent Robotics, Inc., a Delaware corporation. The transaction was done under an Agreement and Plan of Merger dated January 19, 2026, among Serve Robotics, its direct wholly owned subsidiary Delight Merger Sub, Inc., Diligent, and Andrea Thomaz, who acted only as the representative of the indemnifying securityholders. Delight Merger Sub merged into Diligent, and Diligent continued as the surviving corporation and a wholly owned subsidiary of Serve Robotics.

The consideration consisted of Serve Robotics common stock, par value $0.0001 per share, with an aggregate value of $29.0 million, subject to a net debt adjustment, a networking capital adjustment and other adjustments, and that amount includes a potential earnout of $5.3 million payable only if certain milestones are met. At closing, Serve Robotics issued 32,835 shares of its common stock, calculated at $14.3794 per share, which was the volume weighted average price over the 10 trading days before the merger agreement was signed. Up to 366,332 additional shares may be issued later as earnout consideration. Serve Robotics also paid approximately $19.0 million in cash for a debt adjustment, which reduced the stock consideration on a dollar for dollar basis. Serve Robotics assumed 1,319,151 new restricted stock units held by continuing employees, converting them into its own restricted stock units on a one for one basis. Each outstanding share of Diligent common stock was cancelled for no consideration, each outstanding share of Diligent preferred stock was converted into the right to receive Serve Robotics common stock, and all Diligent options and warrants were cancelled for no consideration. The shares issued were sold in private placements exempt from registration under Section 4(a)(2) of the Securities Act of 1933. The filing does not state any interest rate, fees, maturity date, security pledge or guarantee because this was an acquisition paid with stock and cash, not a loan.

The filing does not state what the acquisition will be used for or how it relates to AI infrastructure spending. It only reports that Serve Robotics completed the previously announced acquisition and that the required financial statements and pro forma financial information will be filed no later than 71 calendar days after the date the report was required to be filed. Because the filing gives no purpose, a reader cannot tell from this document alone what the acquisition means for AI infrastructure spending.

On September 24, 2025, AACT and Legacy Kodiak completed the business combination that AACT shareholders had approved at the Extraordinary General Meeting. The filing identifies the combined company as Kodiak AI, Inc. and states that the parties to the Business Combination Agreement completed the transaction on that date.

The filing does not describe a loan, interest rate, fees, maturity, security, or guarantee. It reports that holders of 43,866,808 Class A Ordinary Shares redeemed their shares for cash at approximately $11.45 per share, for aggregate payments of approximately $502.4 million. After those redemptions, $62.9 million from AACT’s trust account was available to the Company following the Closing, before expenses. Immediately after the business combination, there were 181,207,392 shares of Common Stock outstanding, including 30,061,262 SAFE Shares, 7,700,557 Second Lien Conversion Shares, 6,250,000 Sponsor Earn Out Securities, 368,028 Non-Redemption Shares and 1,091,519 Legacy Kodiak Advisor Shares, plus 142,155 shares of Preferred Stock, 55,989,713 Exchanged Kodiak Options, and various warrants and earnout RSUs.

The filing states that the business combination was completed and that $62.9 million from the trust account was available to the Company following the Closing, before expenses, but it does not state a specific use of those proceeds. The filing describes the combined company’s business as autonomous vehicle technology, including the Kodiak Driver and a Driver-as-a-Service business model, but it does not say that the cash is earmarked for AI infrastructure spending. A reader should therefore treat the filing as reporting the closing of the combination and the resulting cash balance, not as a disclosure of new capital expenditure for AI infrastructure.

On April 14, 2025, Intel Corporation and Intel Americas, Inc., as sellers, entered into a transaction agreement with Altera Corporation, then a wholly owned subsidiary of Intel, and an affiliate of Silver Lake, as purchaser. The closing occurred on September 12, 2025. At closing, the Silver Lake affiliate acquired 51% of Altera's equity interests for an equity value of approximately $3.3 billion, and Intel retained the remaining 49%. Intel and the purchaser then each contributed their Altera equity interests to a newly formed limited partnership, and they entered into an amended and restated limited partnership agreement that sets out their rights and responsibilities.

The filing does not state any interest rate, fees, maturity date, collateral, or guarantee. The only financial terms disclosed are the equity value of approximately $3.3 billion for the 51% stake, Intel's retention of 49%, and the contribution of those equity interests to the new limited partnership. The amended and restated limited partnership agreement governs each party's rights and responsibilities, but this filing does not provide further details on those terms.

The filing states that Intel's consolidated financial statements for the third quarter of 2025 will include Altera's results only from June 29, 2025 through September 11, 2025, and after the closing Intel will account for its minority investment under the equity method, meaning Intel will record its share of Altera's net income or loss as a single line item instead of consolidating Altera's full revenue and expenses. Altera's results as a segment of Intel in the first half of 2025 included a gross margin of 55% on revenue of $816 million and operating expenses of $356 million. Intel revised its full-year 2025 non-GAAP operating expense target, which the filing defines as non-GAAP research and development and marketing, general and administrative expenses, to $16.8 billion from $17 billion to reflect the deconsolidation of Altera, while its full-year 2026 target of $16 billion remains unchanged. The filing does not state that the transaction funds AI infrastructure spending; it only reports the divestiture of Altera and the resulting expense target adjustments.

On September 3, 2025, SoundHound, Inc., a Delaware corporation and wholly owned subsidiary of SoundHound AI, Inc., entered into an Agreement and Plan of Merger with Iris Merger Sub, Inc., a Delaware corporation and wholly owned subsidiary of SoundHound, Inc., Interactions Corporation, a Delaware corporation, Shareholder Representative Services LLC, a Colorado limited liability company acting solely as representative of Interactions Corporation's stockholders, and SoundHound AI, Inc. itself for certain provisions. Under the agreement, Iris Merger Sub, Inc. merged with and into Interactions Corporation on the same date, and Interactions Corporation survived as a wholly owned subsidiary of SoundHound, Inc. The acquisition closed on September 3, 2025.

The total consideration was approximately $60 million in cash, called the Upfront Consideration, payable at closing, plus up to $25 million of additional cash consideration to certain stockholders of Interactions Corporation based on certain revenue targets for each of 2026 and 2027, called the Earnout Amount. SoundHound AI, Inc. guaranteed SoundHound, Inc.'s performance of certain obligations under the merger agreement, including payment of the Upfront Consideration and the Earnout Amount. The filing does not state any interest rate, fees, maturity date, or pledged security. From the Upfront Consideration, $150,000 in cash was withheld for 12 months after closing to partially secure the indemnification obligations of Interactions Corporation's stockholders, meaning it can be used to cover certain losses if those stockholders breach their promises. Another $1,000,000 in cash was withheld for post closing adjustments to the Upfront Consideration and will be released after those adjustments are completed. SoundHound AI, Inc. will also establish a customary retention pool for certain continuing employees of Interactions Corporation.

The filing states that at closing, the combined company holds over $270 million of cash on hand with no outstanding debt. The filing does not state what the cash will be used for or any specific AI infrastructure spending. The earnout of up to $25 million is tied to revenue targets for 2026 and 2027, which means part of the purchase price is contingent on future performance. This tells a reader that the deal includes a performance based component, but the filing does not provide further detail on AI infrastructure.

On September 3, 2025, which the filing calls the Closing Date, Unusual Machines, Inc. acquired 100 percent of the capital stock of Rotor Lab Pty Ltd, an Australian company, from its existing shareholders Andrew Robert Simpson and Vella Hardjadinata Corporation Pty Ltd ACN 655 787 367 as a trustee for Vella Hardjadinata Family Trust, together the Sellers. The acquisition was completed under a share purchase agreement dated June 12, 2025, as amended. In exchange, the Company issued 656,642 shares of its common stock as initial consideration, calculated in accordance with the terms of the Agreement, plus the possibility of earnout consideration of up to $3,000,000 worth of shares of common stock.

The filing reports no loan, interest rate, fees, maturity, security, or guarantee because this is a stock acquisition. The initial consideration is 656,642 shares of common stock. Of that amount, 131,328 shares will be subject to possible forfeiture for one year following the Closing Date if there is a breach of representations and warranties and indemnification. The sellers also agreed to be bound by two year noncompete periods following the Closing Date. The initial consideration shares were issued under the Company's effective shelf Registration Statement on Form S-3, Registration Statement No. 333-286413, declared effective by the SEC on April 21, 2025, and a Prospectus Supplement filed with the SEC dated September 2, 2025. The earnout consideration is up to $3,000,000 worth of shares of common stock.

The filing states that Rotor Lab will continue as a wholly owned subsidiary of Unusual Machines and will be used as an engineering hub for motor design and prototyping, complementing the Company's U.S. manufacturing operations. The filing does not state that the acquisition or any proceeds are for AI infrastructure spending. It describes the purpose as motor design and prototyping, which is the only stated use. This tells a reader following AI infrastructure that this particular filing does not report AI infrastructure spending.

On July 15, 2025, Synopsys, Inc., ANSYS, Inc., and ALTA Acquisition Corp., a wholly owned subsidiary of Synopsys, amended their January 15, 2024 merger agreement to change the outside date to August 15, 2025, with an option to extend to November 14, 2025 if certain closing conditions were not met. On July 17, 2025, Synopsys completed the acquisition of Ansys by merging ALTA Acquisition Corp. into Ansys, with Ansys surviving as a wholly owned subsidiary of Synopsys. The merger agreement also required Synopsys to increase its board from nine to eleven directors and appoint Dr. Ajei Gopal and Ravi Vijayaraghavan, and Janet Lee became General Counsel.

Each share of Ansys common stock, par value $0.01, issued and outstanding immediately before the effective time, subject to certain exceptions, was converted into the right to receive 0.3399 of a share of Synopsys common stock and $199.91 in cash, without interest, subject to withholding taxes. Because the aggregate number of Synopsys shares to be issued would have exceeded 19.9999% of Synopsys shares outstanding immediately before the effective time, the exchange ratio was reduced to the minimum extent necessary to stay at or below that maximum, and the per share cash amount was correspondingly increased. No fractional shares were issued, and Ansys stockholders received cash in lieu of fractional shares. Synopsys funded the cash consideration through cash on hand, proceeds from $10.0 billion of senior notes issued on March 17, 2025, and borrowings under a senior unsecured term loan credit agreement. A term loan is a loan that must be repaid over a fixed period, and senior unsecured means it ranks ahead of other unsecured debt but is not backed by specific assets. On July 17, 2025, Synopsys borrowed the full $4.3 billion available under that term loan credit agreement. The filing does not state the interest rate, fees, maturity, or any guarantee for the term loan or the senior notes. Synopsys also terminated approximately $690 million in remaining commitments under a bridge facility, reducing total commitments for the bridge facility to $0.

The filing states that the $4.3 billion term loan was used to fund a portion of the cash consideration, to pay transaction fees and expenses related to the merger, and to repay Ansys' outstanding indebtedness. The $10.0 billion of senior notes and cash on hand also funded the cash consideration. The filing does not mention AI infrastructure spending or any use of the acquisition proceeds for AI infrastructure, so a reader cannot draw conclusions about AI infrastructure from this filing alone.

On July 2, 2025, Hewlett Packard Enterprise Company completed its acquisition of Juniper Networks, Inc. through Jasmine Acquisition Sub, Inc., a merger subsidiary. Under the merger agreement dated January 9, 2024, each outstanding share of Juniper common stock, par value $0.00001 per share, was converted into the right to receive $40.00 in cash, without interest and subject to any required withholding taxes. As a result, Juniper became a wholly owned subsidiary of HPE, and the aggregate merger consideration paid to Juniper stockholders was approximately $13.4 billion.

The filing states that HPE funded the approximately $13.4 billion aggregate merger consideration through a combination of cash from its balance sheet, commercial paper issuances, which are short-term borrowings, and borrowings under two delayed-draw term loan credit facilities: a three-year facility and a 364-day facility. A delayed-draw term loan is a committed loan that the borrower can draw in stages during the availability period rather than taking the full amount at once. The filing does not state an interest rate, fees, a specific maturity date, collateral, or any guarantee for those facilities. It also describes how Juniper equity awards were converted: options became options to purchase HPE common shares, restricted stock units held by non-employee Juniper directors became the right to receive the $40.00 per share merger consideration, and other restricted stock units became time-vesting HPE restricted stock units, with an exchange ratio intended to substantially preserve the value of the awards.

The filing states that the merger closed after HPE and Juniper reached a settlement with the United States Department of Justice on June 28, 2025. That settlement requires the divestiture of HPE's Instant On business and an auction for the non-exclusive licensing of Juniper's Mist AIOps source code used in HPE's WLAN products. The filing does not state any further use of the borrowed funds beyond paying the merger consideration, and it does not describe broader AI infrastructure spending plans. The mention of Mist AIOps source code indicates that the acquired assets include AI operations software for wireless networking, but the filing gives no additional figures or commitments for AI infrastructure.

On May 15, 2025, Richtech Robotics Inc., a Nevada corporation, completed the purchase of a parcel of land of approximately 20,000 square feet located at 2975 Lincoln Road, Las Vegas, Nevada 89115 from L & R Investment LLC, a Utah limited liability company. The purchase was made under a Purchase and Sale Agreement dated April 8, 2025, which had been previously reported on a Form 8-K filed April 14, 2025.

The purchase price was $4,100,000.00, paid entirely with the Company's cash on hand. The filing does not state any interest rate, fees, maturity date, pledged security or guarantee because this was a cash purchase of real estate, not a loan. No borrowing entity or lender is identified.

The filing states that the Company relocated its headquarters to the Property and believes the new headquarters will further integrate the Company's domestic sourcing and assembly operations to satisfy its continued growth. For a reader following AI infrastructure, this shows a robotics company using its own cash to acquire and occupy a physical facility for sourcing and assembly, which is an operational expansion rather than a financing event.

On May 1, 2025, AeroVironment, Inc. completed its acquisition of BlueHalo Financing TopCo, LLC. Archangel Merger Sub LLC, a Delaware limited liability company, merged with and into BlueHalo, and BlueHalo continued as a wholly owned subsidiary of AeroVironment. The seller was BlueHalo Holdings Parent, LLC, the sole member of BlueHalo. On the same date, AeroVironment, as borrower, certain subsidiaries as guarantors, the lenders, and Bank of America, N.A. as administrative agent entered into a Fourth Amendment to Credit Agreement. This amendment added a new $700 million term A loan and increased the revolving commitment to $350,000,000. BlueHalo and certain of its subsidiaries were joined as guarantors to the credit agreement.

The Term A Loan is $700 million, matures two years after May 1, 2025, and amortizes at 5.00 percent per year, with the remaining principal due at maturity. The interest rate is either the Secured Overnight Financing Rate (SOFR) plus a margin of 1.50 to 2.50 percent per year plus a 0.10 percent credit spread adjustment, or the Base Rate plus a margin of 0.50 to 1.50 percent per year, depending on AeroVironment's Consolidated Leverage Ratio. An additional 2.00 percent per year default interest may apply after an event of default. Mandatory prepayments are required for certain asset dispositions not reinvested and for incurrence of non-permitted debt. The loan is guaranteed by the same guarantors and secured by the same collateral as AeroVironment's existing credit facility. AeroVironment must keep its Consolidated Senior Secured Leverage Ratio at or below 3.50 to 1.00 and its Consolidated Fixed Charge Coverage Ratio at or above 1.25 to 1.00. The revolving commitment was increased to $350,000,000, and AeroVironment borrowed approximately $225,000,000 of that amount on the Closing Date. The Amendment also increased certain negative covenant baskets and thresholds, amended the definition of Consolidated EBITDA to include additional add backs, and added materiality qualifiers to certain covenants and events of default. For the merger, all outstanding equity interests of BlueHalo were converted into the right to receive 17,425,849 shares of AeroVironment common stock, par value $0.0001 per share. These shares were issued to BlueHalo Holdings Parent, LLC as the sole member of BlueHalo, which then liquidated and distributed the shares to its equity holders. The shares are subject to lock up restrictions: 40 percent are released on May 1, 2026, 30 percent on November 1, 2026, and the remaining shares on May 1, 2027.

The filing states that the proceeds of the Term A Loan and the $225,000,000 revolving borrowing were used on the Closing Date to repay certain outstanding indebtedness of BlueHalo and to pay for certain related transaction costs. The merger consideration was paid entirely in AeroVironment common stock. This shows that AeroVironment used a combination of new debt and stock to acquire BlueHalo and refinance its debt, which is a significant capital commitment. The filing does not describe BlueHalo's business or any AI infrastructure spending, so no conclusion about AI infrastructure can be drawn from this filing alone.

On August 17, 2026, NVIDIA Corporation entered into a multi-year partnership with SB Energy Corp. and its affiliates, and also entered into multiple residual value guaranties with SB Energy as lessor. The guaranties relate to leases for about 4.25 gigawatts of IT load at the PORTS Technology Campus, a large-scale AI data center campus in Pike County, Ohio, called the Portsmouth Site. An affiliate of OpenAI Group PBC is the tenant under those leases. Through the partnership and the credit support, NVIDIA has secured land, power, and shell capacity at the site to host NVIDIA AI compute infrastructure.

Under the guaranties, NVIDIA's aggregate payment obligation is cumulatively capped at $105 billion for its initial commitment. NVIDIA may also provide credit support for about an additional 3.8 gigawatts at the site, at its sole discretion. The filing does not state an interest rate or fees because these are guaranties, not loans, and it does not describe any collateral pledged as security. A residual value guaranty means NVIDIA promises to cover a shortfall between a guaranteed minimum lease value and what the lessor recovers if the lease fails. NVIDIA must pay only if a trigger event occurs: OpenAI becomes insolvent and defaults under a lease, or OpenAI fails to make lease payments. In that case NVIDIA pays an amount generally equal to the shortfall between the guaranteed minimum value of the lease and amounts recovered through a replacement lease or sale. Upon a trigger event, NVIDIA may assume the lease, require the lessor to relet the premises, start a sale process, allow the lease to be terminated, or defer those remedies for up to one year while paying specified project agreement costs. NVIDIA's obligations end at the earliest of the 20th anniversary of the lease commencement, termination of the lease by OpenAI under its terms, OpenAI achieving a satisfactory credit rating, or other customary termination events. OpenAI has agreed to reimburse and indemnify NVIDIA for any amounts NVIDIA actually pays to the lessor. Payment obligations are also subject to conditions, including the lessor satisfying ready-for-service conditions, expected beginning in 2028.

The filing states that the purpose is to secure land, power, and shell capacity at the Portsmouth Site for NVIDIA AI compute infrastructure. OpenAI, as tenant, will use capacity supporting about 4.25 gigawatts of IT load to deploy NVIDIA's full-stack DSX AI factory platform, subject to limited exceptions. The scale of the commitment, a $105 billion cap, multi-gigawatt capacity, and a possible 20-year obligation, shows that AI infrastructure projects involve very large, long-dated credit support. NVIDIA is providing a residual value guarantee rather than borrowing directly, and OpenAI must reimburse NVIDIA for any payments, which shifts much of the financial risk to the tenant while NVIDIA secures the physical capacity.
